newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone plans deficit budget.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone plans deficit budget.

text.p: Sierra Leone's government has proposed a 1997 budget that foresees a significant deficit despite sharply higher revenue forecasts.

For the financial year beginning January 1, the government plans to spend 163,159 billion leones ($1.75 billion) against revenue of 114,773 billion leones, Finance Minister Thaimu Bangura told parliament on Friday.

Post-war reconstruction and resettlement will take a good chunk of the spending with the budget coming into effect after the government's November 30 accord with rebels ending seven years of civil war. Fighting devastated the mining economy and infrastructure and displaced hundreds of thousands of people.
The government expects to cover the shortfall through borrowing from multilateral agencies, said Bangura, who at the same time lamented Sierra Leone's debt of about $1 billion.
"Debt service as a percentage of merchandise exports for 1996 is estimated at 83.4 percent," the minister said.
"Our monetary policy objective continues to target price stability as a key element in providing sustainable economic growth," he said.

"The record of inflation performance during the year has remained impressive, falling progressively from 38.3 percent in January to 5.6 percent on a year-on-year basis as at the end of November," Bangura said.

The government's medium-term objective is to reduce inflation and broad money growth, hold the budget deficit to below 4.0 percent of GDP and build foreign reserves to 3.7 months of imports, he said. ($=930 leones)
